title: Unified API adoption pathway & client checklist for legacy endpoint consolidation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-level adoption pathway and tactical checklist to guide customers and internal teams through migration from multiple legacy inference endpoints (legacy-complete, v0-stream, legacy-embed-batch) to the Unified Inference API. This doc defines required product changes, client-side helpers, QA gates, communication cadence, and acceptance criteria for marking the consolidation as complete for a given customer cohort.
scope: Define mapping from legacy endpoints to unified API routes and parameter translation rules
Ship client-side migration helper (JS + Python) with opt-in compatibility mode and telemetry hooks
Provide a CLI migration assistant that can test and validate requests against the unified API
Establish telemetry gates (errors, latency, generation-quality drift) and rollout thresholds
Prepare canned migration playbooks for Support and Solutions Engineering with rollback instructions
out_of_scope: Full removal or hard shutdown of legacy endpoints (this is handled in a separate decommission milestone)
Model-level training or retraining to alter response semantics
Customer-specific contract negotiations for reserved capacity pricing
requirements: Server-side: request translation routing layer that accepts legacy payloads and returns identical shape as unified API within compatibility window
SDKs: stable helper functions `migrateRequest()` and `validateMigration()` for Node/Python/Go
CLI: `ri-migrate --test` to run synthetic request/response comparisons and report diffs
Telemetry: auto-tagged metrics per-customer `migration_phase` with buckets: shadow, canary, opt-in, full-rollout
Docs: step-by-step migration guide, sample code snippets, and FAQ with common failure patterns
Support: runbook for Solutions Engineering to assist customers with authentication, model alias mapping, and throttling changes
acceptance_criteria: Translation layer returns 98% success (2xx) parity for legacy traffic shape in shadow mode across 3 representative customers
Client helper libraries successfully translate >95% of top-200 customer call patterns without manual overrides in tests
CLI validation tool finds no semantic diffs for canonical prompt set (1000 prompts) between legacy and unified path beyond allowed variation thresholds
Telemetry gates: no more than 5% relative increase in token latency and <1.5x error rate during canary for a cohort (with rollback if breached)
Support docs published and Solutions Engineering runbook approved by Head of Customer Solutions
Legal notice and deprecation timeframe communicated to customers >=90 days prior to hard decommission
migration_timeline: Phase 0 - Prep (2 weeks): finalize mapping doc, ship SDK helper beta, internal QA
Phase 1 - Shadow (3 weeks): route mirrored legacy requests to translation layer for monitoring; no customer-visible change
Phase 2 - Opt-in (4 weeks): enable opt-in flag for customers; provide CLI/SDK validation and active SE support
Phase 3 - Canary (2 weeks per cohort): roll to small cohorts with telemetry gates and weekly review
Phase 4 - Gradual Rollout (6-10 weeks): increase cohort size with automated throttling policies and customer notifications
Phase 5 - Announcement & Grace Period (90 days): publish formal deprecation timeline and provide assisted migration
Phase 6 - Hard Shutdown (post-grace): execute endpoint turn-down per enterprise agreements
rollout_plan: Create cohort definitions and select 3 pilot customers (one AI-native startup, one mid-market SaaS, one enterprise)
Schedule weekly telemetry review meetings (PM, Eng, SE, Support) during canary
Provide dedicated Slack channel for pilot customers and engineering on-call
Automate feature flag drive to promote cohorts from opt-in to canary to rollout
Enable per-tenant fallback policy that routes failures back to legacy endpoints while preserving SLA billing semantics
rollback_criteria: If token latency increases >25% (absolute) for any cohort over a 15-minute rolling window
If error rate (5xx or response schema mismatches) >2% absolute increase over baseline for 1 hour
If generation-quality regressions exceed thresholds measured by evaluation harness (see design notes) for 3 consecutive daily checks
If customer reports unrecoverable functional regressions where a manual fix is required
telemetry_gates: Per-tenant p50/p95 token latency delta: +10% / +20% allowed in canary
Quality drift: BLEU-like/LLM-specific evaluation score drift tolerated <= 0.03 relative
SDK migration adoption metrics: % of active keys invoking opt-in helper >= 30% by end of opt-in phase
customer_communication: Week 0: Announcement email + migration primer with links to self-serve checklist
During opt-in: targeted messages with CLI/SDK quickstart and offer of SE assistance
30/60/90-day reminders with progress, known issues, and scheduled canary windows
Public changelog entry and dedicated migration landing page with interactive mapping tool
engineering_dependencies: Runtime: translation/compatibility adapter and per-tenant feature flag hooks
SDK: publish helper lib versions and deprecation warnings
Console: migration dashboard surfaces cohort telemetry and per-tenant health
Billing: ensure billing parity while routing traffic across adapters
Observability: tracing enhancements to correlate legacy-request-id -> unified-request-id
design_notes: Design doc: Constrained mapping strategy for query parameters (link below) — prefer conservative translations to avoid changing meaning
Quality evaluation harness: run 1k prompt regression checks and store diffs; manual triage for false positives
UI: add 'Migration status' widget in Console with per-route gating controls for enterprise customers

metrics: Primary: % of total legacy traffic routed through adapter in shadow
Quality: eval harness similarity score (higher is better)
Reliability: per-tenant error rate and p95 latency deltas
Adoption: % of keys using SDK helper or CLI validation tool
risks: Translation layer may mis-handle rare encodings leading to silent behavioral differences
Large customers with custom client implementations may require significant manual effort
Telemetry blind spots could delay detection of quality regressions
Billing parity issues during mixed routing could create customer disputes
